review.evidence: The old bell road crosses the mandatory maps; Split Crown changes from distant paired stones to village frame to physical pass cairn; the quarry track leaves the pass eastward.
All variants retain quarry production, three-valley warnings, the closing slide, a retired chain, and a recent lower tone linked cautiously to west wind and runoff.
Shepherd, keeper, surveyor, and quarry worker have different evidence access without changing the immutable history.
Tables remove shybulb from village/pass, increase elofly with exposure, and return shybulb only in the damp quarry cut.
R2 varies path direction, encounter geometry, settlement circulation, negative space, and quarry density according to the region model.
review.contradiction: The pass remains visually sparse under the frozen vocabulary; this is reported rather than padded.

review.evidence: Initial ordinary topology remained optional-safe; final state naming matches all consumers.
The quarry adds material evidence, potion context, and the hoist shortcut without replacing the ordinary village/pass route.
The four critical paths use different turn sequences and lateral biases, while repeated road/ridge motifs preserve regional continuity.
Split Crown is reused as one regional landform rather than copied as an unrelated prop label.
Road, warning signs, paired stones, civic memory, weather talk, and quarry material recur with different functions.

limitations: Whether first traversal lasts 20–35 minutes for a first-time player.
Whether navigation feels clear moment to moment in the real client.
Whether dialogue feels natural rather than merely fact-consistent.
Whether landmarks are memorable and curiosity feels rewarded.
Whether the low tone interpretation is understood without over-explanation.
